title: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
caption: Info
subtitle: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

title: Icebergs, Ilulissat, Greenland
caption: Info
subtitle: Icebergs, Ilulissat, Greenland
description: Off Greenland's west coast, enormous icebergs drift through the cold waters, creating a landscape that's constantly changing. Many originate from the nearby Jakobshavn Glacier, one of the world's fastest and most active glaciers. The surrounding Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lies about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle. Here, towering blocks of ice break away and begin their slow journey towards the open sea, forming one of Greenland's most remarkable natural sights.

title: Fiddlehead fern
caption: Info
subtitle: Fiddlehead fern
description: Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In mathematics, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

title: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland
caption: Info
subtitle: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Scotland
description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and newer conifer woodlands, with plentiful habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels year-round. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

title: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA
caption: Info
subtitle: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA
description: Snow transforms Utah's Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's most famous overlooks, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, whose limestone was deposited about 50 million years ago and later shaped by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park rises above 2,440 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.

title: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA
caption: Info
subtitle: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA
description:
Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on Hawaii's Big Island. Here, the Wailuku River plunges 24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, that mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name.
Known in Hawaiian as Waiānuenue, meaning ‘rainbow water’, this striking waterfall is also associated with the legend of Hina, mother of the demigod Māui, who is said to have lived in a cave behind the falls, adding another layer of intrigue to this misty landscape.

title: Butte at sunset, Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah, USA
caption: Info
subtitle: Butte at sunset, Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah, USA
description:
Hidden within an ancient sandstone landscape, Face Canyon is one of 96 canyons stretching out from Lake Powell in the US state of Utah. Many are far from roads and would be hard to reach if they hadn't been flooded by the lake, created in 1963 during the construction of the Glen Canyon Dam. The lake's waters back up nearly 300 kilometres, along creeks and canyons which you can explore by boat, kayak or personal watercraft.
Lake Powell took 17 years to fill to the high-water mark and is America's second-largest human-made lake. It is also a contender for most scenic, boasting blue waters surrounded by sandstone walls. You may need to paddle your way to these serene sunset views, but the journey is part of the adventure. And if you arrive when the sun is at its peak, Face Canyon's high cliff walls will provide you with some welcome relief from the desert sun.

title: Old town and Vltava River, Prague, Czechia
caption: Info
description: This autumnal view from Letná Park looks out over Prague, which grew up along the banks of the Vltava River in Czechia. In today's image, the river winds its way through the historic Old Town and Malá Strana districts, beneath Mánes Bridge in the foreground. Many beautiful bridges now span the Vltava, but for centuries there was only one, Charles Bridge, pictured second from the bottom. Its first stones were laid in 1357 during the reign of Charles IV and until 1841, it was the only way to cross the river on foot. Today its stone arches, gothic towers and statues lining the bridge draw large crowds, so tourists are advised to get there by dawn for the best photographs. Or they could walk on to the next crossing, Legion Bridge, which is less crowded and offers beautiful views of the National Theatre, Prague Castle and its busier neighbour.
